rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.e1: The opposition also works on the diagonal: the kings on the same diagonal, with a single square between them, like e6 and g4, with f5 in the middle. With the pawn on d3, the key squares are c5, d5 and e5.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.certo: On c4 your king stands on the same diagonal as the black king, with d5 between them.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.revela: The best is to take the king to c4, on a diagonal with the black king.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.err.c3b2.1: Your king retreats and moves away from c5, d5 and e5.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.err.c3b2.2: The black king goes to d6 and covers c5, d5 and e5.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.err.c3c2.1: Your king retreats and moves away from c5, d5 and e5.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.err.c3c2.2: The black king goes to d6 and covers c5, d5 and e5.

rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.err.c3d2.2: The black king goes to d6 and covers c5, d5 and e5.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.err.c3b3.1: From b3, your king is on the diagonal, but too far from the black king: there is no opposition.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.err.c3b3.2: The black king goes to d6 and controls the three key squares; from b3, your king cannot take the opposition.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.err.c3b4.1: On b4 your king is off the black king's diagonal and does not take the opposition.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.err.c3b4.2: The black king goes to d6 and controls the three key squares; from b4, your king cannot take the opposition.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.err.c3d4.1: On d4 your king is in front of the pawn, but with Black to move: the black king can take the opposition on d6.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.err.c3d4.2: The black king goes to d6 and faces yours: the direct opposition belongs to Black, and it is a draw.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.err.d3d4.1: The pawn advances before the king, and the key squares move up one rank.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.err.d3d4.2: The black king takes d6, among the new key squares c6, d6 and e6.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.livre.fala: Keep playing with White and see how Black defends.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.fins.capturado: The black king captured the pawn, and it is a draw.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.fins.afogado: The black king is stalemated: draw.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.fins.repeticao: The black king always closes the way.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.fins.limite: The black king always closes the way.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.livre.volta: Let's go back to the starting position. Suggest another move or click {verResposta}
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.p: White to move. Think and suggest a move, or click {verResposta}
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.l1: With d5 between the kings, this is the diagonal opposition. As with the direct one, it belongs to whoever is not to move: here, White.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.l3: Black takes the king to d6 and controls c5, d5 and e5.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.l4: You stand face to face on d4: the diagonal opposition becomes direct, and it is still yours. The black king must give way, and your king enters a key square.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.l6: The black king gives way to c6, trying to control c5 and d5.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.l7: Your king gets into e5, a key square. The pawn will promote.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.l8: What if, instead of bringing the king to d4, White pushed the pawn?
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.l9: The pawn advanced too early: the black king stands face to face on c6, with the opposition, and it is a draw. The king goes first, the pawn after.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.l10: Back to the first move: what if the black king went to e5, near the pawn?
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.l11: The black king goes to e5, and your king gets into c5, a key square: once there, White wins.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.l12: What if, with the black king on e5, White pushes the pawn?
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.l12b: It does not work: the black king comes back in front of the pawn, to d6, and it is a draw.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.l14: Back again: kings on the same diagonal, with one square between them. Whoever is not to move has the opposition, and one move makes it direct.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex2.e2: Now the defence, with Black. The white king wants to reach d4, e4 or f4, the pawn's key squares; to close the way, your king also uses the opposition.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex2.certo: On e5 your king is on the white king's diagonal, with f4 between them: the opposition is yours.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex2.revela: The best is to take the king to e5, on a diagonal with the white king: the opposition passes to Black.

rot.diagonal.ideia.ex2.err.e6d7.2: The white king gets into f4, a key square, before your king can control it. The pawn will promote.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex2.err.e6e7.1: Your king retreats, and the white king reaches f4 first.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex2.err.e6e7.2: The white king gets into f4, a key square, before your king can control it. The pawn will promote.

rot.diagonal.ideia.ex2.err.e6d5.2: The white king gets into f4, the key square your king left free, and the pawn will promote.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex2.err.e6f6.1: On f6 your king is off the diagonal, and White takes the opposition.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex2.err.e6f6.2: The white king goes to f4, a key square, facing yours: the direct opposition belongs to White.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex2.err.e6f5.1: Going straight to f5, your king lets White take the opposition.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex2.err.e6f5.2: The white king goes to f3 and faces yours: the direct opposition belongs to White.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex2.livre.fala: Keep playing with Black and see how White attacks.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex2.fins.coroa: The pawn promoted. Without the opposition, Black cannot hold.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex2.fins.limite: The move limit was reached, and it is a draw: the defence held.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex2.fins.repeticao: The position was repeated three times, and it is a draw: the defence held.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex2.fins.capturado: The pawn fell: your king won the fight for the key squares, and it is a draw.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex2.fins.afogado: The black king is stalemated: a draw, and the defence held.

rot.diagonal.ideia.ex2.l1: With White to move, the diagonal opposition belongs to Black: no white move wins.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex2.l2: The white king goes to f3, right next to e4 and f4.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex2.l3: You stand face to face on f5: the diagonal opposition becomes direct, and it is still yours. The white king cannot get through, and it is a draw.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex2.l5: Back to the white king on f3: what if your king went to d4, towards the pawn?
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex2.l6: The white king gets into f4, the key square your king left uncontrolled, and the pawn will promote.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex2.l7: Back to your king on e5, on the diagonal with the white king: when the white king goes to f3, yours goes to f5, face to face, and keeps the opposition.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex2.ponte: Now I play both sides in three positions. See who takes the opposition and whether the attacker reaches a key square.

rot.diagonal.demos.outraAla.2: The white king goes to g3, on a diagonal with the black king. Black is to move: the diagonal opposition belongs to White.
